title: Flip Vertical (ArrangeAndOrganize)

scenarios.title: Flip Vertical applies its documented behavior
scenarios.expected: Flip Vertical (BtnFlipVertical) is invoked on the documented fixture deck and produces its documented effect on the selection or presentation, leaves no new entry in %TEMP%\oPenEfficiency\error_YYYYMMDD.log and does not leave PowerPoint or the add-in in an unstable state.

scenarios.title: Flip Vertical selection scope matches its metadata contract
scenarios.expected: Flip Vertical (BtnFlipVertical, MinSelection=1, RequiredType=Shapes) is at 1 selected shape(s) and above and refused below that, refused for an empty selection and for a slide selection. The scenario asserts that the feature's declared [FeatureMetadata] scope drives the production sidebar enablement decision consistently (metadata -> SidebarStateEvaluator, the declared minimum reachable as an enabled button). It does not execute or inspect the command's own selection guard: an enabled command can still refuse a selection, which is why the guard and the PowerPoint effect stay owned by the office-automated leg.

scenarios.title: BtnFlipVertical deterministic Office leg

requirements.text: In an isolated real PowerPoint host, the deployed Flip Vertical mirrors every selected shape's vertical orientation in place (bounding box center preserved), reports execution, leaves the shapes selected and intact, writes no new error-log entry, and tears down cleanly.

scenarios.expected: In an isolated real PowerPoint host, the deployed Flip Vertical mirrors every selected shape's vertical orientation in place (bounding box center preserved), reports execution, leaves the shapes selected and intact, writes no new error-log entry, and tears down cleanly.

done.statement: The deterministic Office leg passes against the configured build on an isolated PowerPoint host with zero new error-log entries and full teardown; bind-office-evidence-and-reviews remains until this office scenario has real-host evidence and review.
